title: President holds talks with Qatar Emir over regional tensions
byline: Amid escalating tensions in the Middle East, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake held a phone conversation with His Highness the Emir of Qatar to discuss the regional situation and its wider implications, the President’s Media Division said.

title: Sri Lanka on an economic volcano: Harin
byline: Sri Lanka may be sitting on an economic volcano as the Middle East conflict would bring down its foreign remittance, tourism and devaluation of the rupee, a prominent figure in the previous government said yesterday.

title: Global vessel shortage hits Sri Lanka fuel imports amid Middle East crisis
byline: The shortage of vessels amid the Middle East crisis has hampered fuel imports for Sri Lanka, with the government now trying to discourage consumption as much as possible.

title: Fuel prices set to rise again
byline: Fuel prices in Sri Lanka are likely to rise once more by the end of this month or early next month, according to informed sources at the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC).

title: Oil crosses $110 a barrel after gas field strike
byline: Oil prices rose above $110 (£82.78) a barrel after Iranian media reported an airstrike hitting a facility on the world’s largest natural gas field.

title: New system introduced to recover vehicle fuel QR codes
byline: A new method has been introduced from today (March 19) to help vehicle owners retrieve previously registered fuel QR codes when the mobile phone number used for the original registration is no longer in use or belongs to someone else.

title: US intelligence chief says Iran’s regime ’intact’ but ’degraded’
byline: The top intelligence official in the US said on Wednesday that the Iranian regime was ’’intact’’ but ’’largely degraded’’.

title: Labubu movie in the works as viral toys attempt film crossover
byline: The hugely popular Labubu dolls will soon star in their own feature film, Chinese toy company Pop Mart and Sony Pictures have announced.

title: Fuel security under fire, 18-day diesel stock, petrol for 1½ months - Union warns
byline: Fresh controversy has erupted over the country’s fuel reserves after trade unions warned that Sri Lanka has diesel stocks for only about 18 days, despite having the capacity to store enough fuel for nearly three months, while petrol stocks are sufficient for about one and a half months.

title: Frenchman to coach Sri Lanka Sevens team
byline: Sri Lanka Rugby will sign up with former France international and Sevens coach Thierry Janeczek on a six-month deal to prepare the national team for a medal at the upcoming Asian Games in Japan scheduled for October 2026.

title: Former Cricket Secretary rips open Ex-Minister’s conscience
byline: Former Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) secretary Nishantha Ranatunga has conveyed to ex-Sports Minister Navin Dissanayake that what he (Minister) did in 2015 by preventing him (Ranatunga) from contesting an election of office bearers of SLC paved the way for the gradual demise of the national team on the international stage.

title: Iranian footballers return home after dropping Australian asylum bids
byline: Five members of Iran’s national women’s football team who dropped their bids for Australian asylum have returned to the country with the rest of the squad.

title: Nalinda Jayatissa holds talks with Meta to tackle social media misinformation
byline: A special discussion was held today between the Minister of Health and Mass Media, Nalinda Jayatissa, and representatives of Meta to explore practical measures to prevent the spread of misinformation on social media platforms.

title: Sri Lanka faces 5,000 undiagnosed TB cases: Health officials
byline: Sri Lanka continues to battle a significant number of undiagnosed tuberculosis (TB) cases, with around 5,000 patients yet to be identified, health officials warned today.

title: 75 mm showers expected in several areas
byline: Showers exceeding 75 mm are expected at some places in the Central, Sabaragamuwa and Uva Provinces, as well as in the Ampara District, the Department of Meteorology said.

title: Motorists urged to verify identity of vehicle when refuelling
byline: The Department of Motor Traffic has requested motorists to produce either the Vehicle Revenue License, the Vehicle Registration Certificate, the Vehicle Insurance Certificate or the Vehicle Emission Test Certificate to correctly verify the identity of the vehicle when refuelling.

title: Ukraine faces missile shortage due to Middle East war, says Zelensky
byline: Volodymyr Zelensky has said Ukraine will face a deficit of missiles it is using to fight Russia due to the war in the Middle East.

title: 1,000 cataract patients to receive surgery on March 21–22
byline: A special programme to restore vision to 1,000 patients suffering from cataracts will be carried out on March 21 and 22, National Eye Hospital Director Dr. Jayaruwan Bandara said.

title: MPs begin signing no-confidence motion against Power and Energy Minister
byline: Members of Parliament have begun signing the no-confidence motion against Minister of Power and Energy, Kumara Jayakody, sources from the Opposition Leader’s office said today.

title: Restructure CPC loans, grant fuel concession to people: Opposition MP
byline: Opposition MP Dayasiri Jayasekara today urged the government to restructure the debts of Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) and thereby extend the repayment period from 2029.

title: China pledges stronger cooperation with Sri Lanka to crack down on Telecom and online fraud
byline: The Chinese Government says it will continue to strengthen law enforcement cooperation with Sri Lanka to combat telecom and online fraud, following the recent arrest of several foreign suspects, including Chinese nationals, by Sri Lankan authorities.

title: Iran’s parliament speaker says returning women footballers will be welcomed home
byline: Iran’s Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says returning members of Iran’s women’s football team will be embraced by the public.

title: Sri Lanka on “perfect path” to boost Trincomalee tank capacity: Govt.
byline: Sri Lanka is on the perfect path toward increasing the storage capacity of oil tanks in Trincomalee as part of a long-term strategy to strengthen the country’s energy security, Cabinet Spokesman Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said.

title: JR Jayewardene sought $1 million from Mossad for election campaign, document reveals
byline: Declassified documents from Israel’s Foreign Ministry have revealed that former Sri Lankan President Junius Richard Jayewardene had requested $1 million from Israel’s intelligence agency Mossad to finance his election campaign in 1987.

title: Israeli media claim Iran’s intelligence minister targeted in attack on Tehran
byline: Israel’s Channel 12 is reporting Israeli air strikes have targeted Iran’s Intelligence Minister Esmail Khatib.

title: Iran strikes Tel Aviv with cluster warheads in retaliation for killing of security chief
byline: A defiant Iran said Israel’s killing of security chief Ali Larijani and other key officials would not hinder its operations with replacements swiftly appointed, as Israel launched a swathe of strikes against Iran-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon.

title: Namal highlights strategic importance of Indian ocean
byline: SLPP MP Namal Rajapaksa today underscored Sri lanka’s pivotal role in the Indian Ocean during the WION Global Summit, highlighting the island nation’s strategic significance in global trade and security.

title: President urges electric vehicle users to charge their vehicles during daytime
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake yesterday urged electric vehicle users to charge their vehicles during daytime in a move to save electricity.

title: How is Sri Lanka responding to the Israel–Iran conflict: Day 19
byline: As tensions escalate between Israel and Iran, Sri Lanka has taken a series of diplomatic, aviation and precautionary measures to manage potential fallout and safeguard its citizens. Here is how Sri Lanka is responding.

title: Iran launches ‘revenge’ missile attack on Israel after assassinations
byline: Iran has fired deadly cluster missiles at central Israel in what it says is “revenge” for Israel’s assassination of its security chief Ali Larijani, as the war the United States and Israel triggered against Iran rages towards a third week.

title: Sri Lanka among world’s least Happy Nations in 2026 report
byline: Sri Lanka has been ranked among the least happy countries in the latest World Happiness Report 2026, placing 134th out of 147 nations with a score of 4.0, highlighting ongoing concerns over the country’s overall well-being.

title: Pentagon wants $200 billion for Iran war. It’s nearly 50% of Tehran’s GDP
byline: The Pentagon is reportedly seeking over $200 billion from the US Congress to fund President Donald Trump’s war of choice in Iran. If approved, the war funds will boost the US military campaign that began on February 28 and ramp up the production of weapons used during the conflict, according to a report by The Washington Post.

title: No faith motion against Energy Minister handed over to Speaker
byline: The Opposition handed over the no confidence motion against Minister of Power and Energy Kumara Jayakody to Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne today.

title: Cathay suspends Dubai flights until April 30 over Middle East war
byline: Hong Kong aviation giant Cathay Pacific has suspended flights to and from Dubai until the end of April over the war in the Middle East.

title: Filling station in Colombo demands Rs. 3,000 to issue fuel without QR code: MP
byline: A certain filling station in Thimbirigasyaya  had wanted Rs. 3,000 to issue fuel without a QR code from a vehicle owner, MP G.D. Sooriyabandara told Parliament today.

title: Fuel issue hits banana growers?
byline: As Opposition MP B. Ariyawansa revealed that local banana growers are affected by the fuel crisis as the Sinhala New Year draws near, Deputy Minister Namal Karunaratne assured that the government will provide redress to the growers.

title: Trump threatens to ’entirely blow up’ Iran’s largest gas field if it attacks Qatar’s LNG again
byline: Trump has vowed to “blow up the entirety” of Iran’s South Pars gas field if Tehran moves to attack Qatari gas fields again. The warning comes after Iran, in response to an Israeli attack on its gas field, struck Qatar’s largest Ras Laffan facility, sparking global outrage.

title: U.S. special envoy Gor’s travel to Sri Lanka
byline: U.S. Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor will visit Sri Lanka and Maldives from March 19 to 24 for high-level engagements focused on advancing cooperation in the Indian Ocean region. While in Sri Lanka, Special Envoy Gor will meet with senior leaders to reaffirm the importance of the U.S.-Sri Lanka relationship and strengthen cooperation in key sectors.

title: Iran considers levying transit fees on ships in Hormuz Strait, lawmaker says
byline: Iran is considering a proposal to levy transit fees on vessels passing ​through the Strait of Hormuz, a lawmaker ‌said on Thursday, a potential bid to monetise Tehran’s newfound grip over the critical waterway through ​which a fifth of global oil ​and liquefied gas passes.

title: Airbus bribery case: Evidence on warrant request to be heard on March 24
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) informed court that former SriLankan Airlines Board Director Shaminthra Rajapaksa and the suspect’s wife, Priyanka Niyomali, have been named as suspects in the case.

title: Tehran intensifies strikes on gulf energy facilities after Israel hits Iranian gas field
byline: Iran intensified its attacks on its Gulf Arab neighbors’ energy infrastructure Thursday, setting Qatari liquified natural gas facilities ablaze as it hit back following an Israeli attack on its main natural gas field, a major escalation in the Mideast war that has sent global fuel prices soaring.

title: US special representative for South and Central Asia meets President
byline: The United States Special Representative for South and Central Asia, and United States Ambassador to India, Mr Sergio Gor, who is currently visiting Sri Lanka, met with President Anura Kumara Dissanayake this morning (19) at the Presidential Secretariat.

title: No crisis in the country: Deputy Minister
byline: Minister of Labour and Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando said today there is no crisis in the country as some factions are trying to show.

title: Lankadeepa wins SLIM-Kantar People’s Award for 20th time
byline: Wijeya Newspapers ’Lankadeepa’ was named the Most Popular Newspaper of the Year at the prestigious SLIM-Kantar People’s Awards last evening, marking its 20th win at the annual event.

title: Explosive Airbus bribery claim: Rs. 60 Mn allegedly paid to Mahinda Rajapaksa
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption today informed the Colombo Magistrate’s Court that former SriLankan Airlines Chief Executive Officer Kapila Chandrasena had stated, in a statement to the Commission, that a sum of Rs. 60 million received as a bribe in the controversial 2016 Airbus transaction was handed over to then President Mahinda Rajapaksa.

title: Ranil Wickremesinghe’s surgery successful: Ravi K
byline: Former President Ranil Wickremesinghe has undergone a successful surgery abroad, Opposition MP Ravi Karunanayake told Parliament today.

title: Pentagon wants $200 billion for Iran war. It’s nearly 50% of Tehran’s GDP
byline: The Pentagon is reportedly seeking over $200 billion from the US Congress to fund President Donald Trump’s war of choice in Iran. If approved, the war funds will boost the US military campaign that began on February 28 and ramp up the production of weapons used during the conflict, according to a report by The Washington Post.

title: Medical student rescued after falling off World’s End while taking selfie
byline: A 23-year-old female student from the Faculty of Medicine at the University of Colombo was miraculously rescued today, after falling down the precipice at World’s End in Horton Plains National Park. The student reportedly slipped and fell nearly 50 feet while attempting to take a selfie at the edge of the famous viewpoint.

title: Iran floats Hormuz transit tolls as Persian Gulf states warn of military response
byline: Iran is considering charging transit fees on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, a lawmaker said on Thursday, as officials in Tehran stepped up rhetoric over the strategic waterway after this week’s attacks on energy sites in the Persian Gulf.

title: SC rules Wasantha Mudalige’s rights violated by unlawful arrest under PTA
byline: The Supreme Court has declared that the fundamental rights of former Inter University Students’ Federation (IUSF) convener Wasantha Mudalige were violated by the Officer-in-Charge (OIC) of the Peliyagoda Police Station through his unlawful arrest and detention in 2022.

title: President pushes measures to manage fuel prices
byline: A discussion on the economic challenges arising from the ongoing conflict situation in the Middle East and the forward measures required to address them was held this morning (19) at the Presidential Secretariat under the patronage of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake.

title: US objectives in Iran have not changed, Hegseth says
byline: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Thursday that ​the United States’ objectives in the ‌war against Iran have not changed since strikes started on February 28.

title: Bohra funds drive Bambalapitiya Railway Station upgrade
byline: The modernization of the Bambalapitiya Railway Station commenced today (March 19) under a public-private partnership, with significant financial backing from the Dawoodi Bohra community.

title: Japan PM to hold ’difficult’ talks with Trump as Iran conflict looms large
byline: Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is on her way to what she expects will be a ’’very difficult’’ meeting with US leader Donald Trump, days after his calls for allies to help secure the war-stricken Strait of Hormuz went largely unanswered.

title: No faith motion on Energy Minister to be taken up on April 10
byline: Parliament has decided to take up the debate on the no faith motion against Minister of Power and Energy Kumara Jayakody on April 10, 2026.

title: Ex-SriLankan CEO claims he was threatened to involve Mahinda and Namal’s names
byline: Lawyers for former SriLankan Airlines CEO Kapila Chandrasena have released an affidavit stating that his earlier statement to the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption was obtained under alleged intimidation and he was threatened to include the names of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa and MP Namal Rajapaksa in his statement.

title: Government developing Trinco oil tank farm to face global energy crisis: Vijitha
byline: Claiming that no government had taken steps to develop fuel storage capacity to face a global energy crisis, Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath said today the National People’s Power (NPP) government signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with India, Sri Lanka and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to construct a multi-product pipeline and to develop the Trincomalee oil tank farm as an energy hub to face a global energy crisis.

title: Shawwal moon not sighted; Ramadan to complete 30 days
byline: The crescent moon marking the beginning of the Islamic month of Shawwal was not sighted on Thursday (March 19), according to official announcements.

title: Iran floats Hormuz transit tolls as Persian Gulf states warn of military response
byline: Iran is considering charging transit fees on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, a lawmaker said on Thursday, as officials in Tehran stepped up rhetoric over the strategic waterway after this week’s attacks on energy sites in the Persian Gulf.

title: US objectives in Iran have not changed, Hegseth says
byline: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Thursday that ​the United States’ objectives in the ‌war against Iran have not changed since strikes started on February 28.

title: Japan PM to hold ’difficult’ talks with Trump as Iran conflict looms large
byline: Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is on her way to what she expects will be a ’’very difficult’’ meeting with US leader Donald Trump, days after his calls for allies to help secure the war-stricken Strait of Hormuz went largely unanswered.
